title: MEADOW: Memory Efficient Adaptable Dataflow for On-Device LLM Workloads
problem: Running LLM inference on edge FPGAs is severely constrained by the FPGA's limited on-chip SRAM and external DRAM bandwidth, making naive GEMM-based attention execution impractical at the bandwidth envelope of sub-10W devices.
motivation: Edge FPGAs like the Xilinx ZCU102 have <10 TOPS peak and narrow external memory busses; attention's bandwidth requirements dwarf what a single weight-streaming dataflow can achieve, necessitating a co-designed dataflow and weight compression scheme.
method: The system fits LLM inference on power-constrained FPGAs by reorganizing attention calculations and compressing weights. It processes attention by handling multiple tokens (input pieces) in parallel while sequencing through heads (sub-units of attention) one at a time, which keeps all needed data in the chip's fast on-board cache instead of repeatedly fetching from slow external memory. For weight tensors, it identifies repeating chunks and compresses them based on frequency—high-frequency chunks stay lightly compressed for speed, low-frequency ones get aggressively compressed to reduce memory traffic to external storage. All numbers are also stored as 8-bit integers (W8A8 quantization) to minimize the overall memory footprint.
key_novelty: The core contribution is combining token-parallel head-sequential attention processing with frequency-based weight compression (compressing rarely-used weight patterns more aggressively than frequently-used ones) to enable LLM inference on sub-10W FPGAs, achieving 1.5-2.5x speedup over conventional matrix-multiply approaches.
contributions: TPHS dataflow enabling token-level parallelism with head-sequential scheduling to fit attention within FPGA SRAM budget
Three-level weight packing: unique chunk extraction, packet-specific encoding precision, and frequency-aware reindexing
W8A8 quantization pipeline compatible with TPHS dataflow on Xilinx ZCU102
1.5x decode and 2.5x prefill latency reduction vs GEMM baseline; >40% vs CTA and FlightLLM

metrics.speedup: 1.5x decode latency, 2.5x prefill latency vs GEMM baseline; >40% improvement vs CTA/FlightLLM

limitations: Limited to Xilinx ZCU102 FPGA platform; W8A8 quantization may not be sufficient for all model quality requirements; evaluation focused on attention kernels.
